column2: Video checkpoint 1: `nmap -sV -Pn -p T:25565 <public-endpoint>` shows the Minecraft service reachable, the MOTD contains name or student ID, and Grafana shows current node health, pod or workload health, and one Minecraft-specific signal.
column6: All four elements clearly shown: nmap reachability, MOTD with name or student ID, node or workload health panels, and a Minecraft-specific signal visible in Grafana.
column9: Three of four elements clearly shown, or one is ambiguous (for example, MOTD missing name or ID, Grafana missing one signal category, or nmap output incomplete).
column12: No credible baseline observability and reachability demonstration.

column1: Video: Alert definition and runbook linkage (10)
column2: Video checkpoint 2: at least three alert definitions are shown, one alert threshold or trigger condition is explained, and the linked runbook steps for that alert are visible.
column6: All three elements clearly shown: three or more alerts visible, one threshold or trigger condition explained, and linked runbook steps shown.
column9: Two of three elements clearly shown, or one is ambiguous (for example, fewer than three alerts visible, threshold explanation unclear, or runbook linkage not visible).
column12: No credible alert-definition and runbook-linkage demonstration.

column1: Video: Log investigation with kubectl logs (10)
column2: Video checkpoint 3: `kubectl logs` or `kubectl logs --previous` is used to find a specific event relevant to the chosen drill or a recent failure; the log line or event is interpreted; the next investigation step or operator action is stated.
column6: All three elements clearly shown: targeted log lookup, interpretation of the event, and the next operator step stated.
column9: Two of three elements clearly shown, or one is ambiguous (for example, logs shown without interpreting the event, or no next step is stated).

column1: Video: Incident drill detection and recovery (10)
column2: Video checkpoint 4: failure is clearly introduced, detection is shown through a dashboard panel, alert, or log signal, recovery is executed, and the service is confirmed healthy again.
column6: All four elements clearly shown: failure introduced, detection signal shown, recovery executed, and service confirmed healthy again.
column9: Three of four elements clearly shown, or one is ambiguous (for example, failure introduction unclear, detection not visible, or recovery not confirmed).
column12: No credible incident-drill detection and recovery demonstration.

column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) Prometheus and Grafana or equivalent are deployed on the k3s cluster, (2) the deployment and configuration are declarative and version-controlled, (3) both cluster or node metrics and pod or workload metrics are collected successfully, (4) the access pattern is documented and public exposure is minimized or justified.
column6: All four elements present and correctly implemented.
column9: Three of four elements present; one meaningful gap remains.
column12: Two of four elements present; significant missing functionality or weak operational control remains.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or the monitoring stack is not operational.

column1: Dashboard: operator health view and service-specific signal (15)
column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) the dashboard answers "is my service healthy right now?", (2) node health panels are meaningful and labeled, (3) pod or workload health panels are meaningful and labeled, (4) at least one Minecraft-specific signal is collected, visualized, and explained clearly enough for another operator to interpret.
column6: All four elements present and clearly useful to an operator.
column9: Three of four elements present; one panel category or explanation is weak.
column12: Two of four elements present; dashboard coverage is significantly incomplete.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or the dashboard is not usable for operator decisions.

column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) at least three alerts are defined, (2) each alert is tied to a clear symptom rather than an unexplained raw threshold, (3) thresholds or trigger conditions are justified, (4) each alert links to a runbook with first-response steps and at least one alert reflects player-visible service impact or loss of availability.
column6: All four elements present and defensible.
column9: Three of four elements present; one area is weaker or under-justified.
column12: Two of four elements present; significant gaps remain in alert design or runbook linkage.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or the alert set is not operationally meaningful.

column2: Evaluated on five elements: (1) the incident drill report names the introduced failure, detection path, recovery steps, and brief postmortem, (2) kubectl log access and search process are documented clearly, (3) the architecture diagram shows Minecraft, Prometheus, Grafana, exporters, and the existing ECR and S3 integration, (4) the on-call quickstart is actionable for another operator, (5) the repository link or file map and cost controls are complete and usable.
column6: All five items present, accurate, and usable by another operator without clarifying questions.
column9: Four of five items present; one area has a minor but meaningful gap.
column12: Three of five items present; multiple sections are thin or incomplete.
column15: Fewer than three items present or the documentation is not operator-usable.
